nodes.gdpr.concept.pseudonymised_data: Recital 26 is what makes pseudonymised data still personal data; Art. 4(5) only defines the technique.
nodes.gdpr.concept.anonymous_information: Not a defined term in Art. 4; Recital 26 sets the test (identification not reasonably likely by any person).
nodes.gdpr.concept.exporter: 'Exporter' is EDPB terminology, not a GDPR definition; the statutory hook is the controller or processor that transfers.
nodes.hipaa.concept.business_associate: The definition excludes a health care provider receiving disclosures for the individual's treatment (paragraph (4)(i)).
nodes.hipaa.concept.deidentified_information: Two methods: expert determination (b)(1) and safe harbour removal of identifiers (b)(2). A re-identification code is allowed only on the 164.514(c) terms.
nodes.gdpr.cond.art6_1_c_basis_in_law: The national basis is the specific enactment imposing the obligation; none is in the corpus.
nodes.gdpr.cond.art89_safeguards: Shared by gdpr.research_safeguards and route Art. 9(2)(j), so one answer serves both.
nodes.gdpr.cond.third_country_transfer: The GDPR does not define 'transfer'; the EDPB's three cumulative criteria are used to apply Art. 44.
nodes.gdpr.cond.art46_enforceable_rights: Schrems II reads Art. 46(1) as requiring an assessment of whether the transfer tool is effective in the importer's country (EDPB roadmap steps 3-4: transfer impact assessment and supplementary measures).
nodes.hipaa.cond.baa: Shared by hipaa.required_agreements and the business-associate disclosure route.
nodes.hipaa.cond.dua: Shared by hipaa.required_agreements and the limited-data-set route.
nodes.ie.cond.research_governance_and_transpar: Bundled: these measures share one kind of evidence (documented procedures).
nodes.gdpr.route.art9_2_a_explicit_consent: Union or Member State law may provide that consent cannot lift the prohibition; no such Irish provision is in the corpus.
nodes.gdpr.route.art45_adequacy: For the United States the decision is partial: it covers only organisations certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (reference/countries.json).
nodes.gdpr.route.art46_appropriate_safeguards: The route itself is the safeguard instrument (Art. 46(2) or authorised 46(3)); its second conjunct is a separate condition because it is shown by a different document.
nodes.gdpr.dpia: The assessment is activity-based; existing activity alone never proves the DPIA covers the present risks. The Art. 35(10) exemption is explicit.
nodes.gdpr.accountability: Individual rights are covered through the Art. 12(2) duty to facilitate them, not one node per right (Arts. 15-22).
nodes.hipaa.route.research_preparatory: Requires that no PHI is removed from the covered entity, so it rarely fits a cross-border transfer.
nodes.hipaa.route.other_public_interest: The 2025 Purl vacatur affects the 2024 reproductive-health amendments. See reference/legal_status.json; printed text is not sufficient evidence that a provision is operative.
nodes.hipaa.permitted_disclosure: The list does not fully model required disclosures, all special prohibitions, or every permission. Unmodelled alternatives cannot prove permission; failure of listed alternatives alone is not proof that no legal route exists.
nodes.ie.route.explicit_consent: Current wording as substituted by S.I. 18/2021; the corpus also holds the superseded 2018 text.
nodes.ie.route.consent_declaration: Before applying the controller must carry out a DPIA and obtain ethical approval (Reg. 5(3)).
nodes.ie.route.retrospective_chart_review: Limited to the controller's own practitioners and employees; the required notices state the data 'may be used but not disclosed to another person', so it does not appear to cover disclosure to another organisation.
nodes.ie.health_research_measures: Selected consent alternatives are represented. Transitional, capacity and special sector legislation require case-specific review; the graph does not claim this is an exhaustive list.

Both act on another's behalf under a required contract (Art. 28(3); 164.504(e)). Not interchangeable: a business associate can be a GDPR controller for its own purposes, and a covered entity can be a business associate.
correspondences.gdpr.concept.anonymous_information -> hi: Different tests: Recital 26 asks whether anyone is reasonably likely to identify the person; 164.514(b) accepts expert determination or safe-harbour removal of identifiers. Meeting the HIPAA standard does not by itself make data anonymous under the GDPR.
correspondences.gdpr.concept.pseudonymised_data -> hipaa: Both reduce identifiability yet stay regulated: pseudonymised data remain personal data (Recital 26) and a limited data set remains PHI. Their identifier rules differ, so one does not imply the other.
correspondences.gdpr.concept.consent -> hipaa.concept.au: Both are the individual's permission, with different validity rules (Arts. 4(11), 7 and 9(2)(a); 164.508(c) core elements). One does not satisfy the other.
correspondences.gdpr.concept.health_data -> hipaa.concep: Overlapping but distinct scopes: GDPR health data is any personal data revealing health status, whoever holds it; PHI is individually identifiable health information held by a covered entity or business associate.
